summary: - _“1) Condone the delay in completion of subject asset on merit of the same being out of the control of Petitioner in line with CERC Regulations’2019 22(2) “uncontrollable factors” and approve the tariff as claimed._ - _2) Admit the capital cost as claimed in the Petition and approve the Additional Capitalisation incurred/projected to be incurred._ - _4) Allow the petitioner to recover the shortfall or refund the excess Annual Fixed Charges, on account of Return on Equity due to change in applicable Minimum Alternate/Corporate Income Tax rate as per the Income Tax Act, 1961 (as amended from time to time) of the respective financial year directly without making any application before the Commission as provided in Tariff Regulation 2019 as per para 8 above for respective block._ _and pass such other relief as Hon’ble Commission deems fit and appropriate under the circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.”_ - e. The details of the Petitions filed under the instant communication project are 5. The Petitioner has served the Petition on the Respondents and notice regarding filing of this Petition has also been published in the newspapers in accordance with Section 64 of the Electricity Act, 2003. No comments or suggestions have been received from the general public in response to the aforesaid notice published in the newspapers by the Petitioner. Respondent No. 1, Madhya Pradesh Power Management Company Limited (MPPMCL) and Respondent No. 3, Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) have filed their reply vide affidavits dated 21.12.2024 and 16.12.2024, respectively, raising issues of time over-run and GST claim. The Petitioner has filed rejoinder in response to the reply filed by MPPMCL and MSEDCL vide separate affidavits dated 3.1.2025. 6. The hearing in this matter was held on 23.1.2025 and the order was reserved. This order is being passed considering the submissions made by the Petitioner in the Petition vide affidavit dated 11.3.2024 and the Petitioner’s subsequent affidavits dated 12.9.2024 and 6.12.2024, reply filed by MPPMCL and MSEDCL vide affidavits dated 21.12.2024 and 16.12.2024, respectively, and the Petitioner’s rejoinders to the reply of MPPMCL and MSEDCL vide separate affidavits dated 3.1.2025. 8. Having heard the representatives of the Petitioner and perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 14. Further, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 12.9.2024 has submitted that the Commission, vide order dated 27.1.2017 in Petition No. 53/TT/2016 acknowledged that for the assets under a communication system, the CMD’s approval is not required. The same was further reinforced vide corrigendum order dated 7.7.2017, wherein, the Commission has mentioned that CMD’s approval is not required in case of the communication system. 29. The Respondent No. 1, MPPMCL and Respondent No. 3, MSEDCL have submitted that the Petitioner has attributed alleged delay of 1078 days, on account of 30. In response to the MPPMCL’s and MSEDCL’s reply, the Petitioner has submitted that the delay was caused by a severe RoW issues and the event-wise chronology along with supporting documents have been provided in the Petition which significantly hindered the timely progress of the project. Therefore, the delay was due to the circumstances beyond the Petitioner's control, however, all efforts were made to minimise the impact and expedite the work as soon as the conditions allowed. The Petitioner undertook all the reasonable efforts to obtain the necessary RoW clearance with the help of local administration to complete the work as promptly as possible. 37. In response to the MPPMCL’s and MSEDCL’s reply, the Petitioner has reiterated its submissions made in the pleadings. The details of the time over-run with respect to different communication assets considered under the instant Petition are as under: 61. The respondents MPPMCL & MSEDCL have submitted that the time overrun is due to RoW problems, and police protection is squarely the responsibility of the Petitioner. The Petitioner is expected to anticipate such challenges and take necessary steps to mitigate them. The onus to address and resolve these issues rests with the Petitioner, and they cannot form the basis for seeking condonation of delay. 62. The Petitioner in its rejoinder has submitted that the delay due to RoW issues is beyond the control of the petitioner and all efforts were made to minimise the impact and to obtain the necessary RoW clearance with the help of the local administration to complete the work as promptly as possible. 69. We have considered the submission of the Petitioner and the respondents and have perused the submitted documents. The petitioner has submitted Form-12, and the same is extracted as under: 86.
